quarterly_data.signal: First full-year size for the software and services line: SVP of Corporate Development Michael Staiger said 'software and services, I think, in fiscal 2026, we just finished $538 million and growing, so it can be a substantial part of the business', and that it is higher margin. The management stack (SuperCloud Composer, Data Center Manager, Orchestration Manager) is not sold standalone - 'It's part of the solution... It'll go with our systems' - and is the control plane for racks, cooling and storage. New enterprise channel: 'We've integrated that with VCF, and so that's VMware AI Factory', which Staiger called another proof point for reaching more enterprise customers.
quarterly_data.figure: software and services finished fiscal 2026 at $538 million

quarterly_data.signal: Management's own market-size and share math, which it had not laid out before: 'the TAM itself has been segmented out as $2 trillion-$4 trillion... if we're thinking it's $2 trillion-$4 trillion, and we're 10% of that market, and we've said this before, we're 10% now of the market itself... that gives us a $200 billion look'. On ranking: 'if you look at the IDC numbers, our share gain, our position, I think we are number 2. We clearly have sights on number 1.' Staiger argued share gain follows from solutioning rather than being targeted directly, and that the industry is transitioning away from the traditional server / storage / networking compute stack toward application-optimized AI solutions.
quarterly_data.figure: $2 trillion-$4 trillion TAM; 10% now of the market; a $200 billion look; number 2 in IDC share

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity expansion beyond what has been disclosed on the earnings calls. Staiger: 'We have discussed our capacity at 6,000 racks per month, 3,000 liquid cooled, 3,000 air cooled. What we have not disclosed necessarily is the new square footage that we have been adding in Johor, and the new buildings that are coming on stream, and a couple of the clean room facilities, the manufacturing capabilities that we have... We are expanding pretty aggressively under the covers.' He said Supermicro will update the market when those are more solidified.
quarterly_data.figure: 6,000 racks per month, 3,000 liquid cooled, 3,000 air cooled; undisclosed added square footage in Johor plus new buildings and clean room facilities

quarterly_data.signal: Sovereign demand is moving from indirect to direct. Staiger: 'We have more than several sovereign deployments as we speak globally. They're clearly spending. I think the early motion was enterprise spending was into the neoclouds. Sovereign spending was into the neoclouds. We were capturing it early on, but we're seeing clear evidence of them moving forward and putting factories on the floor and expanding there.' Sizing: against the $2 trillion to $4 trillion TAM, sovereigns 'could be a pretty big 10%-25% of the total market', and 'They're fully funded, so they're wonderful in that respect.'
quarterly_data.figure: more than several sovereign deployments globally; sovereigns potentially 10%-25% of the total market

quarterly_data.signal: Structural explanation of the neocloud channel: 'If you think about what's happening at the neocloud level, and you see some of these major contracts where these neoclouds were, many of them and growing, that we're serving, they're getting hyperscaler contracts. In essence, our systems at the neoclouds are serving the hyperscalers. So they need to get those systems up and running immediately.' Deployment scale cited for these operators is '100 to 1,500 rack deployments', where slow stand-up destroys economics (Staiger cited a partner's figure that 8 racks taking 30 days to become operational costs about $3 million). That is the argument for L11/L12 integrated DCBBS racks - power, cooling, CDUs, rear door heat exchangers, storage, switching and software - over shipping bare racks, and for the higher margin content that comes with it.
quarterly_data.figure: 100 to 1,500 rack deployments; 8 racks taking 30 days to stand up costs about $3 million (partner figure cited by management)

quarterly_data.signal: Management restated the scale trajectory in its own terms and dismissed the recurring ODM-displacement concern: 'a couple of years ago we were $1.5 billion, and now we're on our way to doing $15 billion for a year, and now we're on our way to do $15 billion for one quarter and beyond'; 'The order book, obviously, at $60 billion, underpins the guidance for the year.' On the risk that mature neoclouds switch to Taiwanese ODMs: 'That concern was around at $7 billion, at $15 billion, at $22, at $39, and it is going to exist at $68.' He also said '75% growth at these numbers is pretty significant on a year-over-year basis', and that hyperscalers doing their own silicon expands rather than shrinks the number of rack platforms Supermicro must support - fragmentation 'would be difficult to theoretically mass produce'.
quarterly_data.figure: $7 billion, at $15 billion, at $22, at $39, and it is going to exist at $68; 75% growth year-over-year; order book at $60 billion
